name: Item accuracy
what: Correct / incorrect (dichotomous) on a scored item.
usefulness_tail: The base IRT signal; at the tail, accuracy on very hard items is the primary separator once difficulty is high enough to avoid ceiling.
how_to_collect: Log final response vs key per scored item.
how_much_to_collect: >=8-12 scored items per construct per child near the child's ability for a stable theta; more hard items near the cut.

name: Partial-credit (polytomous) score
what: Graded score for multi-step / multi-part items (0..k).
usefulness_tail: Extracts tail information from a single rich item (a partial-credit item behaves like several dichotomous ones), sharpening theta with fewer items.
how_to_collect: Define ordered scoring categories per item; log category reached.
how_much_to_collect: >=4-6 polytomous items per construct; each contributes more information than one dichotomous item.

name: Response time (total)
what: Milliseconds from item onset to submitted answer.
usefulness_tail: Combined with accuracy it separates fast-accurate (able) from slow-accurate; feeds effort-moderated and joint speed-accuracy models.
how_to_collect: Timestamp item render and submit; store ms.
how_much_to_collect: >=20 RT samples per child for a usable per-child RT distribution; log on every item.

name: First-action latency
what: Milliseconds from item onset to the child's first interaction.
usefulness_tail: Indexes planning/encoding before acting; high-ability reflective solvers often show longer first-action latency with fewer revisions.
how_to_collect: Timestamp first pointer/key/drag event.
how_much_to_collect: Every interactive item; >=15 samples for a stable per-child median.

name: Intra-individual RT variability
what: SD or coefficient of variation of RT across items.
usefulness_tail: Consistency (low variability) tracks ability better than peak speed (worst-performance rule); a strong, less-coachable tail signal.
how_to_collect: Compute SD/CV over the child's RT series (correct trials).
how_much_to_collect: >=20-30 RT samples for a reliable CV; do NOT reward raw speed.

name: Lapse rate
what: Frequency / magnitude of the child's slowest responses (worst-performance).
usefulness_tail: The slowest responses, not the fastest, are most diagnostic of ability; fewer lapses => higher ability.
how_to_collect: Take the slowest quartile/decile of RTs; count lapses beyond a threshold.
how_much_to_collect: >=25 trials so the slow tail of the RT distribution is estimable.

name: Revisions / answer changes
what: Count of answer changes, undos, or re-drags before commit.
usefulness_tail: Distinguishes confident tail performers (few, targeted revisions) from guess-and-check; adds process variance beyond right/wrong.
how_to_collect: Increment a counter on each answer change / undo event.
how_much_to_collect: Every item; interpret relative to item difficulty.

name: Solution path / move sequence
what: Ordered sequence of actions taken to reach the answer.
usefulness_tail: Strategy signature: efficient/novel paths mark strong reasoners; supports evidence-model (Bayes-net) scoring that separates HOW, not just WHETHER.
how_to_collect: Append each action {t, action, state} to an event log per item.
how_much_to_collect: Log fully on constructed/interactive items; needs >=5 such items per construct to characterize strategy.

name: Efficiency vs optimal
what: Moves or time used relative to the optimal solution for the item's difficulty.
usefulness_tail: Near-optimal solving at high difficulty is a clean tail separator; catches able children who are also economical.
how_to_collect: Compare M-PATH length/time to a stored optimal for the item.
how_much_to_collect: >=5 items with known optima per construct.

name: Scaffold / hint usage
what: Count and timing of hints or scaffolds the child invokes.
usefulness_tail: Hint-free solving at difficulty is stronger evidence; dynamic-assessment signal (learning rate) can add incremental tail validity.
how_to_collect: Log each hint request with timestamp and item state.
how_much_to_collect: Every item that offers hints; interpret against difficulty.

name: Persistence / time-on-task
what: Time spent engaging a hard item before solving or giving up.
usefulness_tail: Task commitment (Renzulli) is a construct CogAT misses; persistence on hard items adds non-cognitive tail signal and flags disengagement.
how_to_collect: Time from onset to solve/skip on items above the child's level.
how_much_to_collect: >=6 above-level items per child.

name: Error type
what: Classification of errors: near-miss / systematic / random / motor-slip.
usefulness_tail: Near-misses at high difficulty indicate latent ability just below threshold, refining tail placement; filters motor/attention noise.
how_to_collect: Tag the chosen wrong answer against a distractor taxonomy.
how_much_to_collect: Every incorrect response; needs distractors designed with error meaning.

name: Confidence / wager
what: Elicited confidence rating or points wager on the answer.
usefulness_tail: Metacognitive calibration (accuracy of confidence) adds incremental validity and helps down-weight lucky guesses at the tail.
how_to_collect: Optional quick confidence tap or wager after answering.
how_much_to_collect: On a subset (>=8 items) to avoid burden; not every item.

name: Exploration behavior
what: Number of options sampled / states explored before committing.
usefulness_tail: Systematic exploration vs flailing separates strategic tail solvers; useful in open/interactive items.
how_to_collect: Count distinct states/options visited via M-PATH log.
how_much_to_collect: Interactive items only; >=5 per construct.

name: Progress trajectory
what: Partial progress achieved over a multi-step item over time.
usefulness_tail: Turns one hard item into a curve; the shape (fast-to-plateau vs steady) adds tail resolution beyond final score.
how_to_collect: Snapshot state/score at intervals or per sub-step.
how_much_to_collect: Multi-step items; >=4 per construct.

name: Speed-accuracy tradeoff
what: Joint position on the RT x accuracy plane.
usefulness_tail: Models the child's chosen operating point so speed is only credited when accuracy is held; prevents rewarding impulsive fast-wrong responding.
how_to_collect: Pair M-RT with M-ACC per item; fit per-child SAT.
how_much_to_collect: >=20 items with both signals.

name: Ceiling / max difficulty reached
usefulness_tail: Directly probes the tail; adaptive escalation to failure pinpoints the child's edge and is the sharpest single tail statistic.
how_to_collect: Track max b-parameter solved under adaptive escalation.
how_much_to_collect: Requires an item bank extending well above grade level (above-level items).

name: Performance drift (fatigue/engagement)
what: Change in accuracy/RT across the session.
usefulness_tail: Detects disengagement/fatigue that would bias a tail decision; lets scoring discount low-effort late items.
how_to_collect: Regress accuracy/RT on item position within session.
how_much_to_collect: Whole session; needs >=30 items to estimate a slope.

name: Engagement / off-task
what: Idle time, focus loss (blur), and re-engagement latency.
usefulness_tail: Gates all other signals: a tail decision is only valid on engaged responses (supports the 'speed as evidence only when engaged' principle).
how_to_collect: Log window blur/idle timers and time-to-resume.
how_much_to_collect: Continuous background logging across the session.

name: Cross-item consistency
what: Reliability of responses across parallel/equivalent items.
usefulness_tail: Reduces conditional standard error at the cut; inconsistent responders near the cut get more items before a decision.
how_to_collect: Compare responses to matched parallel items (same b, cloned via AIG).
how_much_to_collect: >=3 matched pairs near the child's ability.

name: Post-failure resumption
usefulness_tail: How a child responds to failure (retries, latency to re-attempt, voluntary-quit timing on hard items) is a task-commitment signal invisible to accuracy; near-cut children who re-engage after failure differ meaningfully from those who quit.
how_to_collect: On above-level or near-unsolvable items, log each retry, the latency from failure to next attempt, and any voluntary-quit event with its timestamp.
how_much_to_collect: >=6 hard/near-unsolvable items per child so retry and quit behavior is estimable.

name: Idea fluency
usefulness_tail: Count of distinct valid ideas in an open divergent task; fluency is the most reliable single divergent-thinking index and higher-ability children generate more, providing a continuous creativity axis CogAT lacks.
how_to_collect: Count non-duplicate on-topic responses per prompt (dedupe near-identical entries).
how_much_to_collect: >=3 prompts, roughly 2-3 minutes each, to stabilize the fluency estimate.

name: Category flexibility
usefulness_tail: Number of distinct semantic/functional categories the child moves among; flexibility separates truly divergent thinkers from fluent-but-repetitive ones and is harder to coach than raw count.
how_to_collect: Cluster responses into categories (functional, physical, imaginative) and count distinct categories and switches.
how_much_to_collect: Same open prompts as fluency; needs a category scheme or embedding model.

name: Statistical originality
usefulness_tail: Infrequency of a response against a reference norm bank; rare-but-appropriate ideas are the cleanest creativity tail signal and mark the Renzulli creativity ring.
how_to_collect: Score each response's frequency against a norm corpus; low frequency plus on-topic appropriateness scores as original.
how_much_to_collect: Requires a norm bank per prompt; >=3 prompts per child.

name: Elaboration
usefulness_tail: Amount of detail/embellishment added to an idea or figure (extra words, sub-features, strokes); adds incremental creativity variance beyond how many ideas are produced.
how_to_collect: Count added descriptors/words per verbal idea or strokes/added features per figural response.
how_much_to_collect: Open verbal and figural tasks; interpret relative to time on task.

name: Information-seeking / question count
usefulness_tail: Number and quality of questions asked or information-requests made during a novel activity; a direct behavioral index of epistemic curiosity that reasoning tests miss and that predicts intrinsic drive to learn.
how_to_collect: Count question-card taps or composed questions and rate their depth (surface fact vs causal/why question) during a mystery activity.
how_much_to_collect: >=1 novel exploration activity of 2-3 minutes; more activities improve reliability.

name: Uncertainty preference
usefulness_tail: Proportion of choices for uncertain/novel over certain/known options; a preference for informative uncertainty behaviorally marks curiosity-driven explorers and is hard to fake.
how_to_collect: Present repeated certain-vs-uncertain choices; compute the proportion of uncertain picks and how it shifts as uncertainty is resolved.
how_much_to_collect: >=10 certain-vs-uncertain choice trials per child.

name: Free-choice engagement
usefulness_tail: Time and voluntary actions spent on an activity after the required portion ends and stopping is free; the canonical behavioral intrinsic-motivation measure, avoiding self-report bias and predicting the sustained engagement behind gifted achievement.
how_to_collect: After a 'you're done' gate with an always-visible exit and no rewards, log continued time, count of self-initiated actions, and variety of self-directed play.
how_much_to_collect: >=1 free-choice window of 60-120 seconds; multiple windows across activities improve reliability.

name: Delay-of-gratification wait time
usefulness_tail: Time willingly waited (or the choice to delay) for a larger-later reward; a self-regulation/future-orientation signal that predicts achievement independent of IQ and shows the most variance in young children where reasoning tests are least reliable.
how_to_collect: On a growing-reward wait task with an always-available cash-out, log total wait time, the delay choice, and any strategic self-distraction behaviors.
how_much_to_collect: 1-3 wait trials (a single well-designed trial can be long and informative).

name: Effort allocation ratio
usefulness_tail: Proportion of free time spent on a beneficial-but-tedious task versus an available fun distraction; a behavioral academic-diligence/self-discipline signal that predicts grades beyond IQ and is far less fakeable than conscientiousness self-report.
how_to_collect: In a dual-panel task-vs-distraction block, log time and actions on the diligent task divided by total, plus sustained on-task stretch lengths.
how_much_to_collect: A single 3-5 minute free-allocation block yields a usable ratio; more blocks improve reliability.

name: Rubric-scored product quality
usefulness_tail: Polytomous expert/consensual rating of an open product on originality, reasoning, and elaboration; captures authentic creative-productive giftedness (Renzulli Type III) that keyed items miss and adds ecological tail signal.
how_to_collect: Score the stored product and reflection with an anchored rubric using multiple trained raters; report the mean and inter-rater reliability.
how_much_to_collect: >=1 product per child; >=2 raters per product to establish inter-rater reliability.

name: Careless / invalid self-report flag
usefulness_tail: A validity index for self-report (straight-lining, too-fast responses, inconsistent reverse-coded pairs, infrequency-item failures, social-desirability lean) that gates non-cognitive self-report so faked or careless questionnaires do not distort tail decisions.
how_to_collect: Log per-item response time and response variance, compare reverse-coded pairs for consistency, and check infrequency/attention items; combine into an invalidity score.
how_much_to_collect: Whole questionnaire; requires several reverse-coded pairs and at least one infrequency item.

name: Rule dimensionality solved
what: Number of independent relational rules or attributes the child integrated simultaneously in the correct answer (e.g., a 3x3 matrix solved under three co-acting rules).
usefulness_tail: Separates children by the relational complexity they can bind at once (Halford). Two children may both be correct, but at 1 vs 3 co-acting rules; exposing that structure sharpens tail placement where a single difficulty index blurs it, and it is harder to coach than surface speed.
how_to_collect: Tag each item with its rule set and design distractors so each foil violates exactly one named rule; the chosen option reveals which rule-dimensions were satisfied. Log the maximum simultaneously satisfied rules on correct high-complexity items.
how_much_to_collect: >=6 items whose distractors are orthogonally keyed to individual rules, spanning 1 to 4 co-acting rules near the child's edge.

name: Hypothesis-search efficiency
what: Informativeness of the child's exploratory choices during rule discovery: how quickly errors are eliminated and whether placements test maximally disambiguating cases versus redundant or random ones.
usefulness_tail: In rule-discovery tasks, able children run efficient disambiguating tests and converge fast; this indexes inductive/scientific reasoning and dynamic-assessment learning rate, adding tail signal beyond final accuracy and resisting coaching.
how_to_collect: From the placement/action log, compute the reduction in the viable-rule space per action (or trials-to-criterion after the first informative feedback) and flag perseverative or random tests.
how_much_to_collect: >=1 rule-discovery item with >=6 feedback-bearing actions; aggregate over >=3 such items for a stable rate.

name: Accuracy-gated speed combo
usefulness_tail: Rewards sustained joint speed+accuracy rather than impulsive peak speed; a coach-resistant index of controlled processing efficiency that separates children who hold both at pace from those who trade one for the other.
how_to_collect: Increment a streak on each response meeting BOTH a correctness check and a per-child adaptive RT band; reset to 0 on any error, false alarm, or timeout; store max streak and the streak distribution.
how_much_to_collect: >=30 speeded trials so streak length is estimable.

name: Commission / false-alarm rate
usefulness_tail: Isolates impulsive fast-but-wrong responding so raw speed is never rewarded; separates careful-fast (able) from impulsive-fast responders and underlies the concentration-performance index.
how_to_collect: Count taps on non-target/foil stimuli plus anticipatory responses faster than a plausible floor (<150 ms), divided by response opportunities.
how_much_to_collect: >=40 target/non-target events with a meaningful foil rate (>=30% non-targets).

name: Hick's-law RT slope
usefulness_tail: A device- and base-motor-robust estimate of information-processing RATE: the intercept absorbs motor/device latency while the slope reflects central processing, so it is less confounded than absolute RT at the tail.
how_to_collect: Administer blocks at 1, 2, and 4 response alternatives; regress mean correct RT on log2(N) and store slope and intercept.
how_much_to_collect: >=15 correct trials per set size (>=45 total) for a stable slope.

name: Inspection-time threshold
usefulness_tail: A near motor-free, practice-resistant index of perceptual intake speed - the processing-speed measure with the cleanest (still modest) link to g and the least motor/device confound, making it the most defensible single speed adjunct at the tail.
how_to_collect: Staircase the pre-mask exposure duration (e.g., 2-down/1-up) in a backward-masked two-alternative discrimination and estimate the exposure at the target accuracy (~71-75% correct).
how_much_to_collect: >=40-60 masked trials for a stable staircase threshold; report threshold in ms alongside the measured display frame time.

name: Placement error (percent absolute error)
usefulness_tail: Continuous placement error turns a single number-line item into a fine-grained latent-magnitude signal; small, consistent PAE at hard scales (fractions, wide ranges) separates top reasoners far better than dichotomous accuracy and avoids ceiling.
how_to_collect: Record released position, convert to a value, compute absolute(placed - target) / line-range as a percent per item; also fit the child's placement curve (linear vs log R^2).
how_much_to_collect: >=10-15 placements spanning the scale for a stable PAE and linearity estimate.

name: ANS acuity (Weber fraction)
usefulness_tail: Estimates the finest numerical ratio a child can reliably discriminate; a less-coachable, low-literacy tail signal that keeps separating children when symbolic items would floor or ceiling, especially in K-1.
how_to_collect: Adaptively vary the ratio of the two non-symbolic arrays (staircase), fit a psychometric function to accuracy-by-ratio, and report the Weber fraction w and its standard error.
how_much_to_collect: >=30-40 non-symbolic trials spanning ratios ~1.1 to 2.5 for a stable w.

name: Relational-vs-operational equivalence signature
usefulness_tail: Flags whether a child treats '=' relationally (balances both sides) or operationally (dumps a running total), a research-backed early separator of algebra-ready reasoning that dichotomous accuracy hides; concentrates information exactly where pre-algebraic talent emerges.
how_to_collect: On non-canonical equivalence items, classify the child's first substantive placement/entry against known operational-error targets vs the relational solution, and record whether they self-correct.
how_much_to_collect: >=4-6 non-canonical equivalence items to reliably classify the child's dominant strategy.

name: Proportional strategy signature (multiplicative vs additive)
usefulness_tail: Classifies whether the child preserves the ratio (multiplicative/scaling) or a constant difference (additive) during adjustments, the decisive divide in proportional reasoning that a correct/incorrect score cannot see; isolates genuine proportional reasoners at the tail.
how_to_collect: From the move sequence, fit whether successive adjustments hold the quantity-ratio constant vs the quantity-difference constant, classify the strategy, and record consistency across items.
how_much_to_collect: >=4-6 proportion items including non-integer/non-doubling targets to classify strategy reliably.

name: Mental-rotation RT slope
what: Slope of correct-trial response time regressed on target angular disparity.
usefulness_tail: The classic Shepard-Metzler chronometric signature; a shallow slope held at high accuracy is a rate-of-mental-transformation measure that is hard to coach and finely separates the spatial tail.
how_to_collect: Present matched trials at several angular disparities and regress correct-trial RT on angle per child.
how_much_to_collect: >=12 trials spanning >=3 disparities for a stable slope estimate.

name: Mirror false-alarm rate
what: Rate of selecting an enantiomorph (mirror-image) foil instead of a true rotation.
usefulness_tail: Distinguishes genuine 3D mental rotation from partial feature-matching; low mirror false alarms at high disparity is a clean tail separator.
how_to_collect: Include exact mirror foils and log the chirality of the chosen distractor.
how_much_to_collect: >=8 trials that contain a mirror foil.

name: Perspective-taking angular error
what: Signed angular error between the child's indicated heading/direction and the true direction to the target from an imagined viewpoint.
usefulness_tail: Grades perspective responses far more finely than right/wrong, and its systematic component quantifies residual egocentric bias; low angular error at large viewpoint offsets is a navigation-linked tail signal standard batteries omit.
how_to_collect: On pointing/heading items, record the dial angle and subtract the geometric correct heading; decompose into random and egocentric-bias components.
how_much_to_collect: >=10 pointing trials across a range of viewpoint offsets for a stable error and bias estimate.

name: Lexical frequency ceiling
usefulness_tail: Vocabulary breadth is one of the strongest, most stable verbal-ability correlates; the rarest word-frequency (Zipf) band a child reliably handles separates gifted lexical depth once common words ceiling. An adaptive staircase individualizes the frontier, making it less coachable than a fixed word list.
how_to_collect: Run an adaptive frequency staircase over frequency-tagged word items (receptive vocab, opposites/synonyms, context cloze); record the lowest-frequency (rarest) band answered correctly at criterion.
how_much_to_collect: >=15-20 adaptive vocabulary items spanning several frequency bands to localize the ceiling with acceptable error.

name: Distractor lure profile
usefulness_tail: Which class of distractor (phonological cousin, category/semantic cousin, thematic associate, surface match) pulls a child's errors reveals the grain of their semantic/relational discrimination; category-cousin near-misses at high difficulty indicate latent ability just below the cut, refining placement beyond right/wrong.
how_to_collect: Tag every distractor with a lure class; on each error log the lure class chosen; aggregate the per-child error-by-lure distribution.
how_much_to_collect: Every incorrect response; requires items built with a designed lure taxonomy; >=10-15 errors for a stable profile (pooled across verbal types).

name: Inference depth level reached
usefulness_tail: Comprehension discrimination at the tail is about inference layer, not literal recall; recording the deepest layer answered correctly (literal -> local/bridging inference -> global/thematic -> author's-purpose/evaluative) cleanly separates strong comprehenders who reach evaluative inference from those who plateau at literal.
how_to_collect: Tag each comprehension/absurdity/cloze probe with an inference-depth level; record the maximum level answered correctly at criterion within a passage/unit.
how_much_to_collect: >=4-6 probes spanning depth levels per passage/unit; several passages to stabilize the estimate.

name: Oral-direction condition span
usefulness_tail: The maximum number of simultaneous spoken conditions a child can integrate before dropping one is a sharp, near-language-neutral tail separator that jointly loads receptive language and verbal working memory; gifted children reliably cross-reference 4-5 embedded constraints.
how_to_collect: Adaptive condition-count staircase on following-oral-directions items; record the highest condition count satisfied on all constraints at criterion; log which single condition is dropped on near-misses.
how_much_to_collect: >=12-16 adaptive direction items across condition counts; report span plus the near-miss condition-drop pattern.

name: Memory span threshold
usefulness_tail: The staircase-estimated longest sequence a child reliably reproduces is a continuous, fine-grained capacity index that keeps separating high performers who all hit ceiling on fixed-length items.
how_to_collect: Track the highest sequence length reproduced correctly under a 1-up/1-down span staircase; average the last several reversal lengths.
how_much_to_collect: 6-10 adaptive trials per mode (forward/backward) for a stable threshold.

name: Manipulation cost
usefulness_tail: The drop from forward (storage) span to backward/reorder (manipulation) span isolates central-executive manipulation, which tracks fluid reasoning better than raw storage at the tail.
how_to_collect: Compute forward max span minus backward or sorted max span under matched staircases.
how_much_to_collect: Enough trials in each mode to estimate both spans (6-10 each).

name: Signal-detection sensitivity (d-prime)
usefulness_tail: Separates true match-detection sensitivity from response bias in continuous tasks, so a cautious child and a guesser are not scored alike near the cut.
how_to_collect: From hits and false alarms compute d-prime = z(hit rate) minus z(false-alarm rate) with standard edge corrections.
how_much_to_collect: >=20 target and >=20 non-target trials for a stable estimate.

name: Updating cost
usefulness_tail: The accuracy or RT decrement per additional to-be-updated item or level indexes the efficiency of gating and replacing WM contents, a purer executive signal than static span.
how_to_collect: Regress accuracy (or RT) on memory load / update count and take the slope.
how_much_to_collect: >=4 load levels with several trials each.

name: Post-error adjustment
usefulness_tail: Slowing and accuracy recovery after an error index performance monitoring; adaptive post-error slowing (not rigid or absent) marks metacognitive control at the tail.
how_to_collect: Mean RT on trials immediately after an error minus mean RT after correct trials; also track post-error accuracy.
how_much_to_collect: >=10 error trials with valid following trials.

name: Commission-error rate
usefulness_tail: Failures to withhold on no-go/stop trials index prepotent-response inhibition; low commission rates at high go-probability distinguish strong inhibitory control from impulsivity in a way speed cannot.
how_to_collect: Proportion of no-go/stop trials on which a response was executed.
how_much_to_collect: >=15-20 no-go/stop trials (rare relative to go).

name: Stop-signal reaction time
usefulness_tail: The estimated latency of the covert inhibitory process is one of the least coachable executive metrics; shorter SSRT marks stronger response control at the tail.
how_to_collect: Track stop-signal delay with a staircase and estimate SSRT (median go RT minus mean stop-signal delay).
how_much_to_collect: >=30 go and >=15 stop trials for a usable estimate.

name: Congruency/interference effect
usefulness_tail: Incongruent-minus-congruent RT (flanker/Stroop) isolates interference control independent of baseline speed; a small effect at high accuracy is a strong, hard-to-game tail marker.
how_to_collect: Median RT on incongruent trials minus median RT on congruent trials (correct trials only).
how_much_to_collect: >=20 correct trials per congruency condition.

name: Task-switch cost
usefulness_tail: Switch-trial minus repeat-trial RT/accuracy indexes set-shifting efficiency; low switch cost with maintained accuracy is a clean flexibility signal that fixed-format tests miss.
how_to_collect: Compare RT/accuracy on rule-switch trials vs rule-repeat trials in a mixed block.
how_much_to_collect: >=15 switch and >=15 repeat trials.

name: Perseverative-error rate
usefulness_tail: Continuing to apply the old rule after a switch or silent rule change directly indexes failure to update task set; near-zero perseveration at high difficulty is a sharp executive marker.
how_to_collect: Count post-switch errors whose response matches the previously correct rule.
how_much_to_collect: >=6 post-switch trials per switch across several switches.

name: Processing-task accuracy (complex-span gate)
usefulness_tail: Accuracy on the interleaved processing task gates the validity of the storage score; it detects children who trade away processing to boost recall, protecting tail comparability.
how_to_collect: Proportion correct on the interleaved processing judgments; enforce a minimum (e.g. >=80%) for a valid storage estimate.
how_much_to_collect: All processing trials in a complex-span session (typically >=15).

name: Between-search errors
usefulness_tail: Returning to a location that already yielded a token indexes failure to maintain and update a spatial WM record across searches; few between-errors at large set sizes is a strong tail separator.
how_to_collect: Count revisits to boxes that have already produced a token in a self-ordered search.
how_much_to_collect: Several rounds at set sizes 4-8.

name: Search strategy score
usefulness_tail: The degree to which searches follow a fixed, systematic sequence (few distinct starting boxes) reveals planful strategy use that predicts giftedness beyond error counts.
how_to_collect: Count distinct boxes used to begin each new search (lower = more strategic); log the full move path.
how_much_to_collect: Higher set sizes (>=6 boxes) across several rounds.
